provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — beaconing from user browsers to CDN/analytics-masquerading domains and unexpected outbound JS callbacks are detectable via web-proxy/DNS telemetry against the known watering-hole domains, but the initial profiling blends with normal web traffic
medium — exploitation and SQLi attempts against public-facing apps are observable via WAF/web-server logs and IDS signatures, but attribution to this actor requires corroborating infrastructure
medium — VPN logons with stolen credentials are detectable via authentication analytics (impossible travel, new device/ASN, off-hours) but blend with legitimate remote access
medium — inbound macro-enabled Office attachments are detectable via mail-gateway sandboxing and attachment-type policy, but delivery itself is probabilistic to catch
high — Office applications (EXCEL.EXE/WINWORD.EXE) spawning script interpreters or writing executable content is a high-fidelity child-process detection via EDR process-lineage

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — VBA macro execution spawning child processes / writing files is detectable via AMSI, macro-execution telemetry and Office-to-interpreter process lineage
medium — Python interpreter execution originating from an Office-spawned process and connecting outbound is detectable via process and network telemetry, though Python is common in some environments

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe usage is ubiquitous; value comes from suspicious command-line content and process lineage from implants/Office parents

medium — AppDomainManager hijacking is detectable via unexpected .config files / APPDOMAIN_MANAGER environment variables and anomalous managed-DLL loads into .NET hosts, but requires .NET-aware instrumentation

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation/modification of Run-key values pointing at implant paths is directly observable via registry-modification telemetry (Sysmon EID 13) and autostart auditing
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) and tasks executing binaries from unusual paths are strong detection candidates

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — service installation (Event ID 7045) of an unsigned/unusual binary and service names like WindowsServiceLive are directly observable via service-creation auditing
medium — cross-process/managed-DLL injection is detectable via EDR image-load and injection telemetry, but AppDomainManager loading is subtler than classic CreateRemoteThread injection
high — procdump/comsvcs.dll accessing lsass.exe and writing a dump file is a high-fidelity detection via process-access (Sysmon EID 10) and command-line telemetry
medium — internal scanning bursts and known scanner binaries (netscan.exe, nmap) are detectable via connection-fanout/east-west analytics and process signatures
medium — copying of tool binaries over SMB admin shares and their execution on new hosts is detectable via file-write plus remote-execution telemetry
high — PAExec/PsExec service creation (PAEXEC-* service names, Event ID 7045) and Type-3 admin-share logons (4624/5140) are high-fidelity lateral-movement detections

medium — non-mail-client processes making IMAP/SSL (port 993) connections to consumer webmail (imap.yandex.com) or update-platform-check.online is an anomalous and detectable pattern via network+process correlation, though it hides inside legitimate mail traffic
medium — beaconing to Discord API/webhook endpoints from non-user processes is detectable via proxy/DNS and process correlation, but blends with legitimate Discord usage
high — unsanctioned MeshAgent installation and outbound connections to MeshCentral endpoints are detectable via known-binary/process signatures and RMM-allowlist policy
medium — HTTP(S) callbacks to the known actor domains/IPs are detectable via proxy/DNS blocklisting and JA3/beacon analytics, but HTTPS C2 blends with normal web traffic absent IOC context

medium — outbound IMAP/email uploads from non-mail processes and data volumes to webmail/Discord are detectable via network+process correlation, but exfil hidden in email traffic is challenging to isolate
medium — CDN/analytics-lookalike domains and innocuously named service binaries in unusual paths are detectable via name/path baselining and domain-similarity analytics
medium — high-entropy/encoded payloads and obfuscated script content are detectable via entropy analytics and AMSI script-block logging, but require dedicated scanning
medium — post-foothold downloads from actor domains/IPs and files written after implant callbacks are detectable via network + file-creation telemetry when correlated to known IOCs

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — compromise of third-party/victim-adjacent web servers is off the defender's own endpoints; intel/hunt candidate via web-integrity monitoring and threat-intel on compromised-site infrastructure
low — actor-side staging of drive-by targets occurs on infrastructure the defender does not control; hunt/intel candidate via watering-hole domain intelligence
low — adversary domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via passive DNS, registration-pattern and typosquat monitoring
low — creation of actor webmail accounts is off-victim; intel candidate, though the mailbox addresses themselves are usable network IOCs
low — malware development is off-victim; intel candidate. Downstream execution of the implants is where host detection lands
low — actor-controlled personas live on third-party social platforms; intel/brand-monitoring candidate
low — harvesting credentials from files/config leaves little discrete signal; hunt candidate via file-access telemetry and honeytokens
low — external scanning of the target's perimeter is largely off-victim from an endpoint perspective; medium at the network edge but weakly attributable
low — host-info enumeration is common and low-signal; hunt candidate via recon-burst process-lineage correlation
low — local data collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging patterns and process-lineage context; hunt candidate
